app.subtitle: RPG Maker MV/MZ Project Easy-Click APK Exporter
step1.title: 1. Select project
step1.tooltip: Choose the folder or ZIP archive of your RPG Maker web export. The app will then automatically detect whether it is an MV or MZ project.
step2.title: 2. Confirm engine
step2.tooltip: RPG Maker MV and MZ differ internally in folder structure and scripts. This selection ensures your project is read correctly.
step2.hintDetectedMV: Automatically detected as an RPG Maker MV project. If this is wrong, please correct it manually.
step2.hintDetectedMZ: Automatically detected as an RPG Maker MZ project. If this is wrong, please correct it manually.
step2.hintNotFound: Engine could not be detected automatically. Please choose manually.
step2.logNotDetected: Automatic detection was not conclusive — please choose manually.
step2.logNoIndexHtml: No index.html was found in the selected project.
mvNotice.title: RPG Maker MV Notice
mvNotice.message: Attention! For a successful build, it is recommended to disable the CustomLogo plugin or set the MadeWithMv image to "(none)" in the Plugin Manager.

step3.title: 3. Project name
step3.tooltip: The name later shown as the app name on the device home screen.
step3.label: App name (also used as the folder/build name)
step4.title: 4. Import
step4.tooltip: Copies your project files into a unified working folder that forms the basis for building the app.
step4.hint: Copies the detected project into a unified working folder (www/).
step4.logNoContentRoot: No valid project content root available.
step5.title: 5. App settings
step5.tooltip: Core technical data for your app: unique ID, version, orientation and icon.
step5.packageIdWarnTooltip: The package ID uniquely identifies your app on the Play Store and should not change after publishing — unlike the version number, which increases with every update. Changing the package ID later counts as an entirely new app (existing installs/reviews are lost).
step5.packageIdEmpty: Package ID must not be empty.
step5.packageIdSegments: Needs at least two parts, e.g. "com.company.gamename".
step6.title: 6. Prepare Android project
step6.tooltipQ: Turns your project into a native Android project that can be compiled into a finished APK in the next step. Runs entirely locally, no internet connection needed — the project template is already part of this software.
step6.minSdkTooltip: Defines the minimum Android version your app can be installed on. A lower minimum reaches more devices, a higher one allows newer system features and is often leaner.
step6.hint: Creates the native Android project from a bundled template and sets package ID, app name, icon, orientation and minimum Android version. Runs entirely locally, no internet connection needed.
step6.logInvalidPackageId: Package ID is invalid, please fix it.
step6.logCopyingGameData: Copying game data into the Android project…
step6.logSettingIdentity: Setting package ID, minimum Android version and version data…
step7.title: 7. APK output folder
step7.tooltip: The finished APK file will be placed here after the build. If you don’t choose a folder, a default folder inside the project directory is used.
step8.title: 8. Back up Android project (optional)
step8.tooltip: Saves a copy of the currently generated native Android project (including manifest data) as a ZIP file at a location of your choice. Large, purely regenerable folders (node_modules, Gradle build/cache folders) are excluded to keep the file small.
step8.checkboxLabel: After a successful APK build, the temporarily created project will be removed
step8.hint: Use this to back up the native Android project in advance — especially important if you enable the checkbox above, since then the temporary project folder is automatically deleted after a successful APK build.
step8.logZipping: Creating ZIP archive of the Android project…
step8.logNoProject: No prepared Android project available yet.
log.title: Log
step9.title: 9. Build APK
step9.tooltip: Compiles the prepared Android project with Gradle into a finished, signed APK file that can be installed on Android devices or uploaded to the Play Store.
step9.warnTooltip: The very first time, this step automatically downloads JDK and Android SDK (several hundred MB) and sets them up permanently — independent of any Java/Android SDK you may already have installed on your system. These tools are NOT uninstalled afterwards; future builds simply reuse them. The first run can therefore take several minutes.
step9.hint: The very first time, JDK and Android SDK are downloaded and set up permanently in the background (several hundred MB, can take a few minutes) — on every later run these tools are simply reused, not downloaded again. It also automatically creates a signing key (keystore) for this app the first time. This keystore must stay identical for all future updates of the same app — make sure to back it up via "Zip project" (step 8), especially if you enable the automatic cleanup option below.
step9.logJavaMissing: Java (JDK) was not found. Please install a JDK (version 17 recommended) and make sure "java" is available in the PATH.
step9.logAndroidSdkMissing: Android SDK was not found. Please install the Android SDK command-line tools and set the ANDROID_HOME (or ANDROID_SDK_ROOT) environment variable to the installation folder.
step9.logKeystoreExisting: Found an existing keystore, reusing it.
step9.logKeystoreCreating: Generating a new signing keystore (one-time per app)…
step9.logPatchingGradle: Writing signing and version data into the Android project…
step9.logBuildStart: Starting Gradle build (gradlew assembleRelease)… this can take several minutes the first time.
step9.logApkNotFound: The build finished, but no APK was found at the expected location.
step9.logCopyingApk: Copying the finished APK to the output folder…
step9.logBackingUpKeystore: Also backing up the keystore to the output folder (important for future updates!)…
step9.logNoAndroidProject: Please complete step 6 (prepare Android project) successfully first.
